newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SWISS LIFE WEIGHS FOREIGN LISTING IN FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: SWISS LIFE WEIGHS FOREIGN LISTING IN FUTURE.

text.p: Newly-listed Swiss insurer Swiss Life/Rentenanstalt may consider a listing on a foreign stock exchange, possibly the London Stock Exchange Automated Quotations (SEAQ) system in future, said Manfred Zobl, chairman of Swiss Life Group's corporate executive board.
In an interview with the August edition of Swiss "Invest" magazine, Zobl said Swiss Life's first priority, after its listing earlier this year, would be to focus on bourse trade in Switzerland.
The company's shares began trading on the Swiss stock exchange on July 3 after its members voted in June to convert the former cooperative to a public limited company.

"In the short-term, meaning in the current year and next year, the listing on the EBS (Switzerland's electronic bourse) is the main focus. Then, there is the question as to whether we could make the move 'across the pond' (to the U.S.). We don't want to rule out this step. But we would be considering it at a later phase," Zobl said.
"It is however thoroughly possible that as a next step we would go to SEAQ in London, where most of the shares of large German firms also are traded," he said.
He added because many U.S. investors also trading shares in London, "one doesn't have to be in New York in order to meet (their) needs".
A Swiss Life spokesman, commenting on the interview, said that the firm would likely consider a foreign listing first in the country where the largest number of its investors were based.
